blocks.content: Traffic in human beings and begar and other similar forms of forced labour are prohibited and any contravention of this provision shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.

rows: Prohibition of human trafficking and forced labour
Prohibition of child labour in hazardous employment
Employers in factories, mines, and hazardous work
State can impose compulsory public service

items: Article 23 is available against both the State and private persons, making it a unique fundamental right.
When the State imposes compulsory public service under Article 23, it cannot discriminate on grounds ONLY of religion, race, caste, or class (Note: 'Sex' is not mentioned in this exception clause).
Article 24 does not prohibit the employment of children in harmless or innocent work, though statutory amendments (2016) heavily restrict employment under 14 years across all occupations.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar (forced labour), and other similar forms of forced labour.
Article 23 provides protection against actions of both the State and private individuals.
The State can impose compulsory service for public purposes (e.g., military or social service) under Article 23 without discrimination based only on religion, race, caste, or class.
Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below 14 years of age in any factory, mine, or hazardous occupation.
The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 completely banned the employment of children below 14 years in all occupations and processes.
